title: Choose Brandbeat's new visual world
question: The roll assigned The Specials Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Specials Board
options.lineage: café and bar chalkboards, liquid-chalk-marker menu boards
options.thesis: Your day of music, written up like the board behind the counter: breakfast, lunch, evening, each song with its reason.
options.viewport: A full-height slate board: the venue name lettered big at the top, Morning / Midday / Evening as menu sections in their own marker colour, songs set like dishes with dot leaders to their tempo.
options.risk: Hand-lettering turns kitsch if the type isn't disciplined; the board has to stay a precise tool, not café décor.

raised.raise: Fit is drawn, not printed: a chalk dot's size shows how well each song matches the brand.
State is marked by hand: approved parts get a chalk ring, banned songs a chalk strike-through.
The board is ruled: visible chalk lines grid the days and parts, and everything snaps to them.
Colour discipline: each marker colour means one part of the day, never decoration.
One motion law: everything writes itself on like a chalk stroke.

options.label: The Programme Clock
options.lineage: radio station hour clocks and broadcast cue sheets
options.thesis: Radio programmers already schedule songs, ads and station IDs on a clock wheel; Brandbeat schedules your venue the same way.
options.viewport: A big hour-clock wheel of today's day, segments coloured by part of the day, announcements as notches; beside it the cue sheet of what plays next.
options.risk: Broadcast tropes are familiar to musicians, less so to café owners; the wheel must read instantly or it's decoration.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: The day's music as departures: every song and announcement a row, the next one flipping into place.
options.viewport: The player as a board: NOW, NEXT and the rest of the part of the day in ruled rows, announcements as their own rows.
options.case: Fuses strongly for the player (glanceable at a counter) but weaker for the setup steps, and owners don't see themselves in a station.
options.risk: Setup screens become forms dressed as a board unless the grammar is carried all the way through.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Songs as stars sized by magnitude on a chart of your brand.
options.viewport: A chart of the brand with songs as ranked dots.
options.risk: Pretty but abstract; an owner can't act on a star.
options.case: Loses on both axes: venue owners don't identify with astronomy and the task gets buried.
options.kept: Size carries hierarchy: fit becomes the size of a chalk dot.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Every song a stamp-sized cell you circle in pen.
options.viewport: A packed grid of song cells with circled picks.
options.risk: Too dense for a non-musical owner.
options.case: Loses on both axes for venues.
options.kept: Marking by hand: chalk rings and strike-throughs become the state system.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letters built from a visible grid.
options.viewport: Monumental grid type over a visible armature.
options.risk: A designer's world, not a venue owner's.
options.case: Loses on audience; clarity is fine.
options.kept: The visible ruled grid becomes the board's chalk lines.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: Neutral scale, one accent, every claim proved.
options.viewport: Claim and proof pairs in a strict grid.
options.case: Loses on both axes: it is the generic look the user is asking to leave.
options.kept: Colour discipline: one meaning per colour.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Parts of the day as flat colour lobes on a map.
options.viewport: One lobe per part of the day, coastlines dividing them.
options.risk: Playful to the point of reading as a kids' app.
options.case: Loses on both axes for a business tool.
options.kept: One motion law across the whole product.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean music-business dashboard, like Soundtrack Your Brand or Spotify for business, done properly.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, a grid of playlist tiles and a persistent player bar.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other music app by design.
